**Observed 2026-09-11 17:38 PT, in the CEO's signed-in production session (console v1.6.43), while closing** [DRE-3239](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3239/proof-the-release-train-observed-live-on-the-console-the-unattended)**.** A CRITICAL that clears itself minutes later (a failed release, a refused run) cannot be proven after the fact: the Alerts feed keeps no readable history.

## Already solved

* Raise and resolve each write a structured log line: `console/backend/system_alerts.py:212` (`system-alert raised kind=… severity=… title=…`) and `:288` (`system-alert resolved kind=… severity=… open_since=… title=…`), pinned by `test_system_alerts.py`.
* Marking a system alert done no longer clears it for good (DRE-6762); `alertsTabModel.test.ts:141` asserts the Resolved copy no longer says "for good".

## What to build

1. `alertFeed` grows a `state: OPEN | SNOOZED | RESOLVED | ALL` argument (default OPEN, so nothing today changes) and `UnifiedAlert` grows `resolvedAt`. Today `console/web/schema.graphql:6598` is `alertFeed(offset: Int! = 0, limit: Int! = 20)` and the store serves OPEN rows only (`console/backend/store.py:4353`).
2. The Alerts tab's Resolved view lists resolved alerts (newest first, 30 days) with the Open row shape plus `raisedAt`, `resolvedAt` and the resolution reason ("cleared by run N's successor", "marked done by Sid"). It still says "not on this read" (`alertsTabModel.test.ts:137`).
3. [DRE-3239](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3239/proof-the-release-train-observed-live-on-the-console-the-unattended) rule 7 is answered from the first failed release after this ships, read from the Resolved view.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A resolved alert is readable on the Resolved view and through `alertFeed(state: RESOLVED)` with `raisedAt` and `resolvedAt` (backend test on the feed; vitest on the view)
- [ ] Open-state behaviour, counts and the Needs You tile are unchanged (existing tests stay green)
- [ ] The next failed release's CRITICAL alert is read from the Resolved view and posted on DRE-3239 with PT times

rewrite.draft:
**Repo:** agent-bureau

## What happened

One River is the console's front door. A render throw from one unexpected read (e.g. a `{}` where the SDL promises non-null fields) in its capacity strip, ribbon, routed tab or the card flyout host still reaches only the app-level boundary (`main.tsx:43`), so the CEO sees 'The console failed to draw' instead of one failed panel.

Already solved: `PartBoundary` and `AppBoundary` exist (`components/molecules/PartBoundary.tsx`), and `RunnersPage.tsx:241` wraps its sections in them.

## What to build

* Wrap each One River panel in `PartBoundary`: `CapacityStrip` (`OneRiver.tsx:349`), `Ribbon` (`:380`), the routed tab `<Outlet>` (`:418`, one boundary per tab, reset on route change) and `CardFlyoutHost` (`AppShell.tsx:130`).
* Report a caught throw once through the console's alert path, not only `console.error` (`PartBoundary.tsx:66`).
* Test-first: mount `AppRoutes` with one panel's read stubbed to throw; the other panels and the tile show, and the deep-link dialog still opens.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A throwing panel renders its tile; the page, ribbon and flyout host survive (mount test).
- [ ] The throw is reported once on the alerts path.
- [ ] Design amended per the DESIGNER role decision (2026-09-07) and the design critic passes it.

## Not in this card

* Fixing individual reads' shapes.

rewrite.draft:
**Repo:** bureau-pipeline

## What happened

When a rescue push is refused, agent-task.yml's fallback dispatches a delivery workflow in the product repo. In a repo with no `deliver-rescue.yml`, GitHub answers an App token's dispatch with `HTTP 403: Resource not accessible by integration`, which reads as a permissions problem and is not one. On 2026-09-09 all three of agent-bureau's refusals ended with "the delivery follow-up could NOT be dispatched … so this card needs a human".

**Already solved on main:** the reusable `.github/workflows/deliver-rescue.yml` exists (`workflow_call`, line 49), `self-deliver-rescue.yml` calls it, and README.md:332 documents the product-repo stub.

## What to build

* `scripts/deliver_rescue.py` `handoff()` (the two "could NOT be dispatched" branches, around lines 412 and 429) tells a missing workflow from a refused token. It prints only the last line of GitHub's error today, so the comment says which it is and which fix applies: install the stub, or change the secrets.
* Not checkable from bureau-pipeline's main, so confirm in agent-bureau before building: `scaffold/` carries a `deliver-rescue.yml` stub, `make check-channel-fleet` reports it per repo, and the stub count is ten.
* **[OPERATOR]** install the stub on `main` of every building repo in `config/repo-map.json`, re-run `make check-channel-fleet` and record the rows here.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The "could NOT be dispatched" comment says whether the workflow is missing or the token was refused.
- [ ] A rescue refusal in a product repo with the stub installed ends with `🚚 rescue-delivery-dispatched` and a PR — PROOF on one real run, with run id and PT time.
- [ ] Every building repo in the roster shows the stub present after the operator install.

Rewritten from the groom verify read of 2026-10-11: the reusable workflow and README stub exist, but the dispatch-failure comment still cannot tell a missing workflow from a refused token.
